NEW DELHI: The Gujarat CID has arrested a 25-year-old man from Assam who allegedly masterminded 1,090 cybercrime cases involving Rs 1,071.5 crore across India and maintained links with China-based criminals.The accused, Rafiqul Alam, was arrested by the CID’s cyber cell in Barpeta, Assam, following a technical investigation into an alleged international cybercrime network, according to news agency ANI.Investigators said Alam was allegedly responsible for routing money obtained through cyber fraud, including “digital arrest” scams, through thousands of bank accounts before converting the funds into cryptocurrency and sending them to China.The Gandhinagar-based Cyber Centre of Excellence (CCE) said Alam transferred tainted money through 1,754 bank accounts across India, breaking large amounts into smaller transactions to evade financial surveillance. Police separately said the investigation traced the money to 1,758 accounts.“The money received by the accused through digital arrest or cyber frauds was split and transferred to 1,754 bank accounts across India within an hour by converting large amounts into small amounts to evade the attention of financial surveillance agencies,” the CCE told ANI.Police said Alam was allegedly connected to China-based criminals through WhatsApp and Telegram, where financial information and details of cybercrime operations were exchanged.“The accused exchanged financial information (scanner, user ID, password, crypto wallet, modus operandi of the crime, etc.) directly with Chinese criminals through WhatsApp and Telegram,” the CCE said.Investigators found 23 cryptocurrency wallets on Alam’s mobile phones, through which around Rs 16 crore had been transacted, the CCE said.The agency said the transactions established a link between cryptocurrency and a China-based gang. Investigators also found alleged illegal cryptocurrency trading carried out through the “chip seller” app.“Based on technical analysis and the victims' statement, a team from CCE visited Barpeta city and conducted a three-day recce of the house of the main money launderer in disguise and arrested him along with his technical gadgets,” it said.The CCE described Alam as the alleged “mastermind” of an international gang.“The accused has been involved in a total of 1,090 cyber crimes across the country amounting to Rs 1071.5 crore. His mobile phones also had gaming account transactions,” the Gujarat police unit said.

Article Title: ED: TMC paid little-known company Rs 160 crore to buy a jet & helicopter
Article Text:
ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company.

NEW DELHI: An ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company has found that the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore from the party's coffers to a little-known firm, Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd, to buy an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC for Rs 187 crore.Sources said the money laundering probe was focused on TMC providing an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore to the aviation company, which had no funds to buy the jet and the chopper it then gave to the party on rent. As soon as it received the security deposit, Carewell Aviation transferred it to its offshore entity, Carewell Flyjet IFSC Pvt Ltd, registered in Gujarat's Gift City, treated as foreign territory, for further purchase of the jet and the helicopter.Another fund transfer of over Rs 16 crore from Cayman Island and related to the deal is under investigation.TMC was required to pay Rs 186.9 crore, exclusive of GST, for using the jet over 72 months and the chopper for 56 months. Although it did not fully utilise the minimum guaranteed flying hours under the charter agreement, the party went on to hire aircraft and helicopters from other companies during this period (2021-26) for a sum of Rs 149 crore, sources said.When contacted, a TMC source said, "Since the matter is sub judice, we do not want to comment."The "suspicious" nature of transactions has led ED to delve into the issue of why TMC paid an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore when it had to pay charges for renting the aircraft and helicopter. The agreement provided that TMC pay a minimum monthly charge of Rs 90 lakh for the aircraft and Rs 60 lakh for the helicopter.Carewell Aviation came into being only a few months after TMC returned to office for the third time after the April 2021 assembly elections. Then, after losing the assembly polls in 2026, TMC paid three months advance rental to the company to cover the period till Sept 2026: something that the agency says is contrary to the norm.Sources said ED has questioned directors of Carewell Aviation over these transactions and recorded their statements on issues such as why it charged TMC Rs 16.5 lakh per flying hour for the jet and when it billed others, who had not helped it with something as crucial as a security deposit, a much lower amount of Rs 7.6 lakh per hour for flying Embraer.Investigations also showed, sources said, that TMC paid Rs 75 lakh per flying hour to another charter service, Windborne Aviation, for hiring a Falcon 2000 aircraft. TMC used the Falcon aircraft for only about 11-12 flying hours but paid Rs 9.1 crore, which was roughly Rs 75.7 lakh per flying hour.According to sources, the money trail showed that over Rs 160 crore was transferred to Carewell Aviation and its group entities between July 2021 and June 2026 for "charter services" for the Embraer aircraft and the Agusta chopper. Investigators suspect the transaction to be an "artificial commercial arrangement" and a "calculated device", bereft of any genuine actual financial rationale, considering that the two aircraft were allegedly purchased entirely out of the corpus received from TMC, and the two aviation assets were rented back to the party.The jet was purchased two months after the charter agreement was signed and security deposit provided. Similarly, the charter agreement for the VIP helicopter was signed by TMC in March 2025 while the chopper was purchased a month later in April.Carewell Aviation, which was incorporated on Sept 14, 2021, with Pawan Jaju and Ramesh Jaju as its directors, purchased the Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft on June 6, 2023, and the Agusta 109 Grand helicopter on April 17, 2025, using its offshore entity.
Article Summary: ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company. Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore to a little-known firm. Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd bought an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC.

NEW DELHI:Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law amid a row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event which snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of the graduates before retracting with regret.Hours after addressing VCs of national law universities at Jodhpur, CJI Kant told TOI he "never consented to Nalsar's invitation" to be chief guest at the convocation."The question of me attending the convocation does not arise," CJI said. Four days ago, Nalsar confirmed it had, in keeping with tradition, invited CJI Kant to be chief guest at the ceremony that is likely to be held at the end of Aug or in Sept.Of Nalsar's 1,400-odd students, more than 400 had opposed CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his remarks during a hearing on petitions related to the students' march to Parliament on July 20 and alleged police excesses.The CJI-led bench is seized of a bunch of petitions seeking independent inquiry into the alleged police excesses on students, use of pellet guns and facial recognition devices for profiling students in alleged breach of right to privacy.It has also accepted a petition by the relatives of injured police personnel seeking strict action against "criminal elements" who infiltrated the students' agitation and caused widespread violence and damage to public property while abusing PM and other constitutional functionaries.The students appeared to have taken umbrage at the CJI-led bench declining to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged police excesses against protesters when an advocate, without filing a proper petition, made the request on July 22, claiming he had video footage of the same. The CJI had asked him to file a proper petition articulating his allegations.However, when the advocate, without producing a scrap of a paper, persisted with his request that the bench watch the videos, the CJI, with a heavy cache of cases already before him, had asked him not to waste judicial time and suggested he file a proper petition.Petitions raising similar concerns were subsequently filed and entertained by the CJI-led bench, which had asked police not to take any coercive action against students and preserve all video and CCTV camera footage as well as sought suggestions for an independent inquiry into the incident and setting up a commission to lay down pan-India guidelines for graded action by police to control protests turning violent.The controversy over students' opposition to the invite to CJI snowballed after BCI chairperson, Manan Kumar Mishra, unilaterally issued a letter to the Nalsar vice-chancellor seeking an inquiry and identification of students who opposed the CJI's presence at the convocation and threatened to debar them from getting registered as advocates.Faced with condemnation, BCI quickly withdrew the circular. SC has sought its response while observing that the regulator had no business wading into a matter which concerned CJI and Nalsar students.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law. The row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of graduates.

Article Title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this August
Article Text:
Julie Sweet asks employees to help deliver a strong fourth quarter

Why Accenture changed its vacation policy

AI remains a key concern for Accenture investors

Accenture CEO Julie Sweet is asking employees to think twice before taking time off this August as the company pushes for a strong finish to its financial year. In a rare one-time policy change, Accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year instead of requiring them to use the leave before August ends. The move comes alongside Julie Sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue in the final weeks of the quarter after the consulting giant reported weaker-than-expected quarterly results. Accenture’s new policy will give its workers more flexibility while helping keep more employees available during the company's year-end sales push.In a memo seen by Bloomberg, Accenture CEO Sweet urged employees to contribute to improving fourth-quarter results by finding new ways to serve clients and generate revenue. "Our shareholders are counting on us to deliver a strong quarter in Q4 — everyone can contribute," Sweet wrote.“This means we all need to find more ways to serve clients that create more revenue in the quarter and to originate more sales (small, large, mega) to finish strong,” she added.According to Bloomberg, the company has also allowed employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next financial year, which begins on September 1.Normally, staff must use their vacation before the fiscal year ends.People familiar with the matter told the publication that the temporary policy change is part of the company's effort to keep more employees working during August rather than taking leave before their vacation days expire. Another person familiar with the matter said the one-time change is also meant to give employees greater flexibility.The move comes after weaker-than-expected results. Accenture reported a 2% decline in new bookings for the quarter ended May 31 and projected fourth-quarter revenue of $17.75 billion to $18.4 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $18.47 billion. Following the earnings announcement in June, Accenture shares fell about 20% in one day, one of the company's biggest single-day declines on record.The earnings report also intensified concerns that artificial intelligence could disrupt the consulting industry in the near term, even though Julie Sweet has described AI as a "tailwind" for Accenture's business.Bloomberg Intelligence said in a recent research note: “AI remains the dominant concern for services and consulting. Though management positions Accenture as a long-term AI beneficiary, tangible evidence that AI is accelerating demand is limited.”
Article Summary: Accenture will allow staff to carry forward any unused vacation days into the next fiscal year instead of requiring them to use the leave before August ends. The move comes alongside Julie Sweet's call for employees to focus on winning new business and generating more revenue in the final weeks of the quarter.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Gautam Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive. He has more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting. His appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.

Article Title: In 2020, Minnesota funded a $1.918 million Shell Rock River habitat program; by 2025, it had protected or restored 588 acres
Article Text:
Shell Rock River Watershed District (Image Credit: www.shellrock.org)

A habitat program takes shape

Three properties protected

Wetlands and prairie restored

More acres than planned

A longer-term conservation effort

In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. According to a 2025 final report from the Lessard-Sams Outdoor Heritage Council, the program ultimately protected, restored or enhanced 588 acres of habitat in the Shell Rock River watershed, exceeding its original goal of 483 acres.The funding was provided under Minnesota Laws 2020, with the appropriation directed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources for an agreement with the Shell Rock River Watershed District. The funding was intended to support land acquisition as well as the restoration and enhancement of aquatic habitat within the watershed. The program focused on several types of conservation work, including acquiring properties, restoring wetlands and improving aquatic habitat. The projects were selected using conservation planning and monitoring intended to identify areas where habitat improvements could provide significant benefits.The Shell Rock River Watershed is a shallow-lake system that supports fish, waterfowl and other wildlife. According to the final report, restoration projects were targeted at addressing habitat degradation and improving conditions for native fish, waterfowl and wildlife.One part of Phase IX involved acquiring three properties: the Glenville Property, the Bancroft Property, and the Church Lake Property. The District closed on the Glenville Property in March 2021 and the Bancroft Property in September 2021. For the Church Lake Property, the District transferred the deed to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources in December 2024 after acquiring and restoring the parcel.The final report says these acquisitions contributed to the program's permanent protection of 218 acres. Another 370 acres of habitat and wetlands were enhanced or restored through the program. Together, those accomplishments contributed to the reported total of 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.The program included several restoration projects beyond property acquisition. The Bancroft Wetland Restoration was initiated in 2020, with construction beginning in June 2024 and largely completed by the fall of that year. Additional seeding work was completed in spring 2025. Another project focused on Panicum Prairie, where habitat enhancement work was carried out across 300 acres. The project involved native prairie vegetation and was substantially completed in February 2025, with final work completed in May.The program also supported the Fountain Lake In-Lake Habitat Project. Work included additional rock reefs and rock boulder clusters intended to improve fish habitat. The report notes that Phase IX funds were used to expand the scope of this work after the District determined additional funds were available. These projects addressed different parts of the watershed's ecosystem, from wetlands and prairie habitat to aquatic areas. The broader aim was to improve habitat conditions while protecting areas that could provide long-term benefits for wildlife.The program's original accomplishment plan called for 483 acres. By the end of the project, the final total had reached 588 acres, 105 acres more than initially planned. The report attributes the increase to the addition of the In-Lake Habitat Project and the Church Lake Property to Phase IX.According to the report, all grant funds were spent. The final grant expenditure remained $1.918 million, while the program's final total including leverage was $1.9479 million.The work is intended to continue beyond the end of the grant. The Shell Rock River Watershed District relies on multiple funding sources, including a local option sales tax, local levy and public funding, to maintain conservation projects. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources will also maintain the Church Lake Property, which it owns.The program's results illustrate how a single state-funded conservation effort can combine land protection, wetland restoration, prairie enhancement and aquatic habitat improvements. Rather than focusing on one habitat type, Phase IX combined several projects across the Shell Rock River watershed. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored. The completed work represents a combination of permanent land protection and habitat improvements designed to support Minnesota's fish, waterfowl and wildlife over the long term.
Article Summary: In 2020, Minnesota approved $1.918 million for the Shell Rock River Watershed Habitat Restoration Program - Phase IX. By 2025, the program had moved beyond its original target, with the final report recording 588 acres protected, enhanced or restored.

Article Title: Biggest US grid operator has a ‘shutdown proposal’ that shows tension between data centers and power grids in America
Article Text:
Representative image

Why grid operators are worried with rapid expansion of datacenters

PJM Interconnection, the largest electrical grid operator in the US, has proposed a framework that would require data centers to switch to backup generators when regional power reserves hit dangerously low levels. According to a report in Reuters, the proposal aligns with President Donald Trump's "Ratepayer Protection Pledge," a non-binding initiative aimed at shielding residential consumers from escalating costs tied to surging data center power demands, according to PJM.Under the proposed emergency procedure, utilities would be instructed to curtail or transfer electricity demand from data centers and other heavy energy consumers before imposing blackouts on residential households. This means that PJM Interconnection is proposing a shutdown of data centers in emergencies. In the event that the power grid is in danger of shutting down, they want data centers to be shut down first.However, PJM noted that it currently lacks direct authority to mandate such curtailments and must rely on cooperation from individual state regulators.PJM manages electricity distribution for 67 million people across a 13-state region stretching from Washington, D.C.to Chicago. The move underscores intensifying friction between the rapid expansion of energy-hungry data infrastructure and the capacity of the aging U.S. power grid.The grid operator's recent capacity auction saw prices hit a regulatory cap of $325 per megawatt-day. Despite those price signals designed to spur new power generation, PJM still faced a roughly 6.8-gigawatt shortfall against its projected reliability requirements, heightening the risk of system-wide blackouts.To better manage system loads, PJM is also seeking to establish a registry to monitor the locations and power consumption of data centers and other massive electricity users. The rapid proliferation of data facilities has evolved into a contentious political issue across PJM's footprint, notably in Northern Virginia, which hosts the world's largest concentration of data hubs. Local communities increasingly voice concerns over noise, neighborhood disruption, and the risk of absorbing the utility bills required to power the tech sector's expansion.
Article Summary: PJM Interconnection, the largest electrical grid operator in the US, has proposed a framework that would require data centers to switch to backup generators when regional power reserves hit dangerously low levels. The move underscores intensifying friction between the rapid expansion of energy-hungry data infrastructure and the capacity of the aging power grid.

Article Title: Why Google is making headlines in Berkshire's biggest quarter of stock-buying following Warren Buffett's exit as CEO
Article Text:
Warren Buffett ’s legacy and Abel’s role

Other portfolio changes

Cash deployment

Berkshire Hathway has sharply increased its stake in Alphabet during its biggest quarter of stock buying in years. According to a report by Business Insider, under CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire boosted its holdings by 83% to about 106 million shares worth $38 billion at the end of June in Alphabet. The conglomerate agreed to purchase $10 billion worth of Alphabet stock at a discount in a private placement in June, and added another 19.6 million shares on the open market last quarter. Alphabet is now Berkshire’s third‑largest US holding, behind Apple ($66 billion) and American Express ($51 billion).The size of the Alphabet bet stands out given Buffett's long-standing reluctance to invest heavily in technology stocks throughout most of his career, with Apple as the notable exception. He has historically preferred businesses like Coca-Cola and Geico over tech names. Even so, Buffett has said he personally made the call to invest in Alphabet last year, and with Abel now serving as CEO while Buffett remains chairman, the position appears to reflect shared decision-making between the two rather than a clean break from Buffett's past preferences.Alphabet's stock has climbed roughly 170% over the past three years, with investors continuing to bet that the search-and-advertising giant will emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the ongoing AI boom.Alphabet wasn't the only shift in Berkshire's holdings last quarter. The firm boosted its stake in Delta Air Lines by 44%, bringing that position to $5.4 billion as of June 30. It also established a new stake in D.R. Horton and added significantly to its existing positions in Lennar and Macy's.On the other side of the ledger, Berkshire roughly halved its stakes in Capital One and Nucor, trimmed its holdings in Bank of America and Kroger, and exited a smaller position in Constellation Brands entirely.The second‑quarter update showed Berkshire spent $23.5 billion on stocks while selling only $3.7 billion, ending 14 straight quarters as a net seller. It also executed $4.5 billion in buybacks, reducing its cash pile from $380 billion to $365 billion.
Article Summary: Alphabet is now Berkshire’s third‑largest US holding, behind Apple ($66 billion) and American Express ($51 billion) The firm also boosted its stake in Delta Air Lines by 44%, bringing that position to $5.4 billion as of June 30.

Article Title: US green card approvals drop 35%, Indians hit hardest; what US immigration authority data says
Article Text:
Most decline is among Indian technology workers

Tighter US immigration policies

Alternatives and shifts

US green card approvals witnessed a 35% drop and Indians are the hardest hit, as reported by Economic Times. The approval rate for EB-1A green cards, the US route for extraordinary-skilled workers has dropped sharply in FY26, with Indians facing the steepest impact. As reported by ET, the data from Boundless Immigration, based on USCIS fillings, show approvals for Indians fell to 35% in the first two quarters of FY26, down from 49.1% in FY25.* FY25: Indians filed 14,250 petitions; 6,993 approved, 1,474 denied.* FY26 (first two quarters): Indians filed 7,316 petitions; 2,571 approved, 1,131 denied.Immigration experts say the decline is most pronounced among Indian technology workers, followed by Chinese applicants, who file the largest EB‑1A volumes.The drop comes amid tighter US immigration policies under the Trump administration. Joel Yanovich, Senior Attorney at Ganey Law Group, said adjudicators are demanding an “unreasonably high bar,” despite no change in law. “The spike in denials is not due to a drop in the calibre of applicants,” he noted.Boundless CEO Xiao Wang added that meeting three of the ten USCIS criteria is no longer sufficient. Strong evidence in categories such as leading roles in distinguished organizations and commanding high salaries is now considered baseline, with one additional high‑quality criterion required.With EB‑2 and EB‑3 backlogs stretching up to 15 years, Indian nationals are exploring alternatives:* EB‑1C: Working abroad for a year as a manager/executive.* EB‑5: Investment‑based route, seeing a surge in Indian applicants.* Relocation to Canada or the UK, where talent visas are more accessible.Immigration attorney Rajiv Khanna said adjudications have become “extremely difficult,” despite courts questioning the methodology. Experts warn that unless policy shifts, extraordinary‑skilled workers — especially Indians — will continue to face hurdles in securing permanent residence in the US.
Article Summary: US green card approvals witnessed a 35% drop and Indians are the hardest hit. The approval rate for EB-1A green cards, the US route for extraordinary-skilled workers has dropped sharply in FY26. The drop comes amid tighter US immigration policies under the Trump administration.

Article Title: Elon Musk-owned Tesla to launch Cybercab robotaxi service in Austin this month; employees to get first ride
Article Text:
Tesla to launch Cybercab robotaxi service this month

Tesla began Cybercab production in June

Tesla has already started Cybercab rides in Austin

Tesla faces competition from Waymo

Elon Musk-owned electric car maker Tesla has reportedly told its employees that it will soon announce the public launch of Cybercab – its self-driving taxi service powered by AI and full self-driving tech. According to a report by The Information, the service will be first rolled out in Austin, Texas as early as this month. As per the report, Tesla is planning to initially offer the Cybercab rides to its employees on public roads before adding the vehicles to its robotaxi service just days later. The EV car manufacturer has been preparing for the potential launch through several stages of testing. The company has reportedly conducted test drives, given employees rides on private roads and trained local first responders ahead of a possible public rollout.According to The Information report, Tesla began testing the production version of the Cybercab on public roads in June. Production of the vehicle is expected to increase later this year. The Cybercab is designed specifically for autonomous driving and does not have conventional driving controls such as a steering wheel or pedals. However, Tesla Board Chair Robyn Denholm said last year that the company remains open to equipping the vehicle with traditional controls.Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja said during the company's second-quarter earnings call that the company had already started testing the Cybercab at its Austin factory. "We’ve started doing Cybercab rides in our factory in Austin," Taneja said.A wider launch on public roads would mark a major step for Tesla's robotaxi plans, which CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly presented as an important part of the company's future.Tesla's planned Cybercab rollout comes as Alphabet's Waymo continues to expand its driverless robotaxi business. Waymo recently received approval in California to expand its driverless ride-hailing service across the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles, while also entering Sacramento and San Diego. The company now provides more than 500,000 fully autonomous electric rides each week and has completed more than 220 million rider-only autonomous miles.Tesla is also expanding its robotaxi operations beyond Austin, with services planned in Dallas and Houston.
Article Summary: Elon Musk-owned electric car maker Tesla has reportedly told its employees that it will soon announce the public launch of Cybercab – its self-driving taxi service. According to a report by The Information, the service will be first rolled out in Austin, Texas as early as this month. As per the report, Tesla is planning to initially offer the cybercab rides to its employees on public roads before adding the vehicles to its robotaxi service just days later.

Article Title: Jamie Dimon has 'job loss message' for UK chancellor, days after sending public warning to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham
Article Text:
JPMorgan CEO Ja​mie Dimon

Jamie Dimon's pattern of lobbying against bank taxes

Public warning to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham

Why banks could be a target

Other bank leaders weigh in

Jamie Dimon, CEO of America’s biggest bank JPMorgan Chase has cautioned UK chancellor John Healey against creating a more hostile tax environment for banks. According to a report by Financial Times, in a recent call, Dimon said that higher taxes often drive jobs elsewhere, citing a decline in finance roles in New York that he attributed partly to the city’s tax burden. One person familiar with the exchange said Dimon made clear that a windfall levy on bank profits, or broader tax increases targeting wealth, would not be welcomed by the industry. Another person familiar with the call said Dimon told Healey that the only real path to solving the UK's economic challenges was through growth, and that growth could only come through good policy.The comments made by Dimon come as the financial services sector prepares for a major pre‑Budget lobbying campaign. Banks are seen as a tempting target for Healey, given bumper profits and union calls for higher taxes to fund household energy bill relief. Dimon made clear that a windfall levy on bank profits or wider wealth taxes would be unwelcome.Dimon was among the bank chiefs who successfully lobbied against higher taxes ahead of last year’s Budget, holding talks with then chancellor Rachel Reeves as JPMorgan weighed plans for a new £3bn London base at Canary Wharf.A person close to those negotiations said Dimon “always majors on the impact of bank taxes” and will want assurances that a Burnham government supports the new HQ.Dimon’s private comments follow a public warning last month to Prime Minister Andy Burnham, when he said higher bank taxes could have “adverse consequences.” He noted that JPMorgan shareholders had already paid $5bn in extra taxes under the UK’s post‑2008 regime.One person close to Dimon's earlier negotiations with Reeves said he consistently emphasizes the impact of bank taxes and would likely want reassurance that a Burnham-led government would continue backing the new Canary Wharf headquarters. Asked whether Dimon had previously threatened to cancel the planned office over higher bank taxes during talks with Reeves, the person said "threatened" was too strong a characterization, though they noted that any business naturally weighs the fiscal environment before finalizing investment decisions. JPMorgan had revealed its plans for a new building at its Riverside development in Canary Wharf the day after Reeves' Budget, noting at the time that the project would depend on a continuing positive business environment in the UK.Rules introduced after the 2008 financial crisis already require UK banks to pay additional taxes beyond standard corporation tax, including a levy on their balance sheets and a surcharge on profits. But with bank profits having surged in recent years due to higher interest rates, there is concern within the City that lenders could become a target for an even tougher tax regime. The Trades Union Congress has specifically urged Healey to raise the surcharge banks pay, currently set at 3% above the 25% corporation tax rate, to help fund cost-of-living support for households.Dimon isn't alone in pushing back. Santander chief Ana Botín told the FT in June that the UK's bank tax regime made no economic sense, suggesting that if policymakers were looking for sectors earning outsized returns, there were other places to look first. Separately, senior officials from Sir Keir Starmer's former Labour administration have urged Healey this week not to derail the UK's economic recovery through higher business taxes or a significant expansion of borrowing. Miles Celic, chief executive of lobby group TheCityUK, said ministers and officials need to treat the private sector as a partner in attracting investment and boosting growth, working with industry rather than imposing on it.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned UK chancellor John Healey against creating a more hostile tax environment for banks. Dimon said that higher taxes often drive jobs elsewhere, citing a decline in finance roles in New York that he attributed partly to the city’s tax burden.

Article Title: Iran war risk: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warns of oil shocks, sticky inflation and higher interest rates
Article Text: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has warned that the ongoing war in Iran could trigger oil and commodity price shocks, keeping inflation elevated and pushing interest rates higher than current market expectations, Reuters reported.The warning came in his annual letter to shareholders, a day after US President Donald Trump escalated pressure on Iran by threatening to target key infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened."Now, because of the war in Iran, we additionally face the potential for significant ongoing oil and commodity price shocks, along with the reshaping of global supply chains, which may lead to stickier inflation and ultimately higher interest rates than markets currently expect," Dimon said, news agency Reuters quoted as saying.Dimon, who has led JPMorgan for two decades, also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China."The challenges we all face are significant," he added.He said it remains uncertain whether the Iran war will achieve US objectives, while warning that nuclear proliferation remains the biggest risk linked to Iran.Markets have already begun pricing in these risks, with expectations of interest rate cuts this year largely fading amid rising inflation concerns triggered by the conflict.Last week, the benchmark S&P 500 index recorded its worst quarterly performance since 2022, weighed down by rising energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty since late February.Dimon noted that the US economy remains resilient, with consumers continuing to earn and spend, and businesses staying broadly healthy, though signs of weakening have emerged.He cautioned that economic strength has been supported by significant government deficit spending and past stimulus, while infrastructure investment needs continue to grow.At the same time, he pointed to positives such as fiscal stimulus under President Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill", deregulation policies and rising capital expenditure driven by artificial intelligence.On financial stability, Dimon said the $1.8-trillion private credit market "probably" does not pose a systemic risk, despite investor concerns and recent withdrawals from such funds.However, he warned that in a downturn, losses across leveraged lending could exceed expectations as credit standards have weakened.Private credit markets also lack transparency and rigorous valuation benchmarks, increasing the risk of investor exits if conditions worsen, he said.Separately, Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical" and "very flawed".He said JPMorgan’s GSIB surcharge would fall only to 5.0%, a level he described as “absurd” and “un-American”, arguing it penalises the bank’s scale and performance.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns Iran war could trigger oil and commodity price shocks. He also highlighted broader geopolitical risks, including the war in Ukraine, tensions in the Middle East and friction with China. Dimon criticised revised US capital rules, including Basel III and GSIB surcharge norms, calling aspects of the proposals "nonsensical"
